title: nccw-1998-world-heavyweight-championship
label: "Dominator" Don Cameron

won.source: A 2005-11-07 PWW announce-booth résumé calls him NCCW's "first ever world heavyweight champion" (citing PWW's own Weekend of Steel II coverage); the 1998 RSPWF Top 200 (already served, /promotions/rspwf/archive/top-200-1998.html) tags him NCCW at #81 the same year the fed opened. No document records the originating match.

how: Became the fed's own first World Heavyweight Champion at or near NCCW's May 1998 founding; the winning match itself is not recovered.
note: Loses the title to “Supreme Destroyer” Katis, 4 July 1998, per the fed's own titles page.

how: Defeated “Dominator” Don Cameron for the World Heavyweight Championship, per the fed's own titles page.

title: nccw-1998-world-heavyweight-championship

how: Regained the title at some point after the fed's own dated record ends (the last confirmed champion is “Phenomenon” Tyro Marvel, per Battle in Seattle, 7 August 1999); not regained directly from Assassin, as the fed's own titles page shows four further champions between Assassin's reign and the fed's own record's end.
note: The historical record breaks off here: the same reminiscence states this reign led into "a huge feud" with Lew Spectre, but no document records a further title change, a defense, or how NCCW's own World Title era ended before the fed folded c. 2000/01. Recorded as an open gap, not resolved.
